newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle Atlantis closes in on Russia's Mir. [CORRECTED 19:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Shuttle Atlantis closes in on Russia's Mir. [CORRECTED 19:35 GMT]

text.p: Shuttle Atlantis on Wednesday neared the end of a three-day chase through space to reach the Russian space station Mir and pick up U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid.
The shuttle was within 2,500 miles (4,000 km) of the orbiting space outpost by Wednesday morning and was closing the gap by 400 miles (643 km) with every 90-minute revolution around the Earth.
Atlantis was headed for Mir to pick up Lucid, in her fifth month aboard the station, and drop off her replacement, John Blaha, for a four-month stay.
The shuttle, making its fourth visit, was due to dock with the 10-year-old station at 10:13 p.m. CDT (0313 GMT on Thursday), slightly earlier than originally planned. (Corrects GMT time conversion)
"We're sure anxious to see Shannon looking out the window in Mir," said Atlantis astronaut Tom Akers.
The shuttle's six astronauts were awakened on Tuesday evening by a recording of "Rescue Me" sung by Fontella Bass.
"A message from Shannon," joked mission control's Kay Hire.

Lucid, a 53-year-old biochemist, arrived at Mir in March and expected the shuttle to bring her home in early August. But rocket problems, a hurricane and a scheduling clash with an unmanned rocket delayed her return by nearly seven weeks.

Shuttle commander Bill Readdy, pilot Terry Wilcutt and mission specialists Blaha, Akers, Jay Apt and Carl Walz made last-minute preparations on Wednesday for their arrival at Mir. They tested the shuttle's docking system and filled containers with drinking water for the Mir crew.

The astronauts were to begin their final approach to Mir about 7:30 p.m. CDT (2430 GMT). With Readdy at the controls, Atlantis will inch closer to the station, carefully avoiding the station's forest of delicate, electricity-generating solar panels. A final nudge from the shuttle's manoeuvring jets will link the two spacecraft as they soar high above Russia.
If all goes according to plan, the hatches between the two craft will swing open about 12:39 a.m. CDT (0539 GMT) on Thursday.
The first order of business will be for Lucid and Blaha to swap places.
Blaha, a 54-year-old former fighter pilot, will remain aboard Mir with Russian cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Kaleri until Atlantis returns in January to retrieve him.
Blaha was to be the second of six U.S. astronauts to join Russian crews aboard the Mir into 1998.
The two spacecraft will remain joined in space for five days while the astronauts transfer thousands of pounds (km) of equipment and supplies to and from Mir.
